# AgentMandaat

> Governance for AI agents in Dutch SMBs (MKB, 20–200 employees): record what each agent may do, have the agent check that mandate before every action, and keep a hash-chained audit log that others can verify themselves.

Status: pilot phase. There is a working demo with a fictional company; no product for sale and no customers yet. Netherlands first. Under Dutch law an AI agent is not a legal person: this is internal governance and delegation, not a power of attorney (volmacht) to the agent.

Site: agentmandaat.nl (preview, not indexed). This file is the agent-facing summary.

## What the demo does

- Mandate: scope (allowed and prohibited actions), systems, amount limits per action and per month, who approves, accountable person, validity. Templates: procurement, email on behalf of the company, CRM changes, HR (prepare only). Output as JSON and as a PDF to sign by hand, with a content hash.
- Check before every action: the agent asks first and gets allow, needs approval (a human decides on an approval page; the decision is sent back by webhook) or deny, always with a reason. Integration via HTTP API, webhook (e.g. n8n) or MCP.
- Audit log: every check and decision is a hash-chained entry. Export as CSV, JSON or PDF. A standalone page lets a third party re-verify the chain without the AgentMandaat server. The latest hash can be downloaded or mailed daily to keep a copy outside the system.
- Revoke: one button; afterwards every check is denied and pending approvals expire.

## What it is not

- Not a power of attorney for the agent and not legal advice.
- Not a certification and not a claim of AI Act compliance.
- No claim that the log is legally valid evidence; whether insurers, buyers or accountants accept it is what the pilot tests. The PDF has no electronic signature.
- It only enforces where the agent can call a check before acting. AI built into a software package without such a hook is covered by the mandate as a document only.
